reviews.title: No free version, you have to pay
reviews.text:
There is no free version of this app. It only gives you a 3-day free trail, and then it forces you to take a Quartly (49.99 every 3 months) or yearly (69.99 a year) subscription. No per month option. Especially now with everything so expensive, an app subscription is not necessary and most people can not afford those prices.

They should either make a per month option or a free version with ads. Don’t bother with this app

reviews.title: Had no idea what I was missing
reviews.text: After reading a book titled Breath, I realized there were some major things I was missing in my day-to-day breathing and specifically during my workouts. I found this app which not only helps raise my CO2 tolerance but also made me a plan that supports hrv recovery for after my workout. This helps my body get out of stress mode much quicker and activates my parasympathetic nervous system. I tried a few different breathing apps but this has been my favorite. I love the "sciencey bits" that explain how everything is working and why they do it the way they do. It also offered more of a challenge, and more results than any other one I've seen.

reviews.title: Very expensive beta
reviews.text:
I like this concept, and I like some of the Breathwork classes. But the fact that they think it’s ok to charge that much money annually for what appears to me to be an app not really ready for prime time is absurd. I see reviews from a year ago saying there are random bugs…there still are. And most egregious, they only support Apple Watch, which frankly at this point at least in my world, no one really has anymore. If you have anything else, you have to go through this crazy connection process before EVERY class that I pretty much immediately gave up on. AND it appears that if you have an Oura, you’re out of luck, not even a workaround for you. Are these people for real? They’ve been promising this for quite awhile too, based on reviews.

It’s also, frankly, basically the same class morning and night. Yes slightly different teacher or whatever but I’m not sure ultimately what I’d be paying for that I couldn’t get by choosing two Breathwork YouTube videos and just doing them for free every day. Especially given their wearable situation.

I’ll do my trial, apparently it’s a miracle I got more than 3 days based on reviews. But I’ve already set it to cancel. This app frankly doesn’t deserve payment yet, and the fact that its team thinks this is ok is alarming.

reviews.title: I had doubts but it’s awesome
reviews.text: I’ve always had trouble “breathing in through the nose and out through the mouth” when running so decided to give this a try and I am amazed. After 6 weeks of doing the recommended program running is easier, my average HRV is up by 15+ points, and my average RHR is down several. I also use the sleep-related sessions to fall asleep faster and get back to sleep when I wake in the middle of the night. I really appreciate the practical focus on breathing separate from other issues or programs. Highly recommend it!

reviews.title: Mostly good, with some major performance bugs

But since this app does not work with Garmin I have never been able to sync the hear rate feature (which is the metric used to measure progress) to it. It says it works with Garmin, but it have not ever once picked up my Fenix 8 or my hrm chest strap. I’d recommend finding free breath work on YouTube.

I was excited to start but don’t want to risk only having 48 hours to get a feel for the program before deciding to commit or be on the hook for that charge. reviews.title: Very expensive and repetitive workouts
reviews.text: I was inundated with ads for this app, but there was only a 3-day free trial and you can’t pay monthly for the subscription. So, paying almost $50 for a quarterly subscription seemed ridiculous. I ended up trying it on a whim after a run. 30 days was enough to see that this is not worth the money for me. The first 30 days was mostly repeating the same 3-4 workouts every day. By the end of the first week, I knew the script for each workout by heart. You definitely do not need anyone coaching you through these workouts and saying, “You got this, team!” It was the most expensive app I’ve ever purchased, and I learned my lesson.

reviews.title: Charged $96 before 3-day trial expired
reviews.text:
Very predatory trial scheme. 
I had a very disappointing experience with this app and its trial process. 

To even access the app, you’re required to sign up for a subscription ($45 every three months or $90 annually), which is presented with a three-day free trial. I set a reminder on my phone if I wanted to cancel before the trial ended, but was charged BEFORE THE THREE-DAY TRIAL WAS OVER. I also never received the reminder notification that the app indicated I would receive before the trial expired. 

The set up was frustrating from the beginning. The app requires an email verification code to log in, but I never received the code with my primary email address. I ultimately had to use a Gmail account just to access the app. 

Even after getting in, I was only able to use the app for one, five minute session. I couldn’t get it to connect with my Apple Watch despite multiple attempts. Before I even had a fair chance to evaluate whether the app worked as advertised (or worked for me, personally), I was charged for the annual subscription—$96.

I’m currently waiting for Apple to process a refund because I should not have been charged before the trial period ended, especially given the technical issues that prevented me from properly using the app. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend it.

reviews.title: Unusable without subscription
reviews.text: In an age where every developer is forcing you to subscribe for even the most basic features, this app is no different. I shouldn’t be surprised, but I was hopeful to at least experience a taste of what the app has to offer without being forced to subscribe. Alas, you can’t even get to the home page without saying yes. Instantly deleted.

reviews.title: Looks Good So Far with One Caveat
reviews.text:
I have been interested in breath work to improve my athletic performance for a while now. Most of the apps I’ve seen are little more than glorified meditation apps with maybe an exercise or two to increase endurance buried somewhere behind a bunch of menus. 

I saw an ad for FivePointFive declaring it is a breath work app for athletes and I had to try it. So far, the breathing exercises I’ve done are unlike any of the ones I’ve seen in other apps and I am cautiously optimistic that they will help improve my performance. I also like that it built a personalized 90-day plan for me…I find it much easier to stick with something long term when I have a plan.

I do have one significant concern that prevents me from giving the app a perfect 5 stars though. The performance section which displays all of your data and progress only works if you have an Apple Watch. One of the major selling points of this app is that it uses your wearable to provide feedback. There is a workaround where you can broadcast your heart rate from your Garmin or other smartwatch and an AI coach will give you feedback on the class you just completed, but there is no way to view consolidated data along with long term trends. Garmin support is supposedly coming soon and I’ll be happy to amend my rating when that happens.

I don’t know if its the breath work or my exercise routine but I’m sold!

reviews.title: Helpful guidance with a science-backed plan
reviews.text:
I had a coach point out to me that you can live for up to a couple weeks without food, days without water, but only minutes without air. Breathing well is critical not just for performance and growth but overall health.

So I’ve been interested in breath work for a while but it was hard to find a simple and clear process to follow to see actual results. Five Point Five has filled that void. I now have a plan to follow and the consistency is paying off. I just finished my 200th session and notice a difference in my runs as well as my rest and recovery. It takes daily commitment, but the commitment is worth the investment. If you’re looking to dial in your breathing and take your performance and health to the next level, commit to a 90-day session and do the work…you won’t regret it.

reviews.title: Game changer!
reviews.text: We’re halfway through 2026 and downloading FivePointFive remains the single best thing I’ve done for myself this year.  Nearly 200 classes in, I’m now breathing comfortably (through my nose!) on my runs as well as better managing my anxiety as it arises. This app is a game changer for your physical AND mental health - double duty I honestly didn’t expect. The training is simple, effective, science-based, and all guided by genuinely likable coaches who almost seem to become friends you look forward to checking in with each day. I cannot recommend it enough.

reviews.title: Great app! Will renew, and use it!
reviews.text:
Like many others, I have tried loads of apps, and bailed on them. Danielle sent me a message when I asked what the best way to utilize the app is, and what classes to do when, how often etc…

I got such a detailed response that I am looking forward to adding the routine to my daily routine, and making breathwork a part of life. This isn’t just to learn how to breathe. It’s to work with physiological processes, sleep, relaxation and all of which breathwork can help!

The company cares and wants to improve your quality of life, and they show it in action. Don’t be afraid to ask questions!
